Turkish society places significant emphasis on hospitality through food and beverage sharing, with customs such as sharing tea or coffee forming key aspects of hospitality. Meals are often family-centered, and guests are traditionally offered food or drink as a sign of respect and generosity. Turkish tea, coffee, and raki transcend their culinary purposes and are often associated with ritual, conversation, and social bonding, serving as focal points for social interaction and relationship-building. Coffee is one of the fundamental pillars of hospitality in Turkish tradition. Serving coffee accompanied by lokum and water shows respect to the guest and reflects the principles of generosity at the center of Turkish social traditions.
